context.why: Stories 1 and 2 are accepted: a registration names a place (navigation, action, card), PluginRegistry.resolve(model) works out the mounts a record type serves, and URL patterns, the navigation, the page actions and the cards are all built from the mounts (fairdm/contrib/plugins/registration.py, checks.py, places.py, cards.py). This story lets a portal or an addon take a registered plugin away from one record type: plugins.remove(Model, plugin). A removed plugin contributes no mount, so it has no address, entry, action or card there, and its name does not resolve. The result must be the same whether the removal is declared before or after the plugin is registered. The part most likely to be missed is the pages FairDM ships that link to a plugin by name: each must be served without the link, and without an error, when the plugin is gone.
spec_sections: Edge Cases (a plugin both removed and replaced is US4's; a removed address answers as if it never existed)
Out of scope (no redirect from a removed address)
prior_decisions: decisions.md D1: removals are kept as declared, per record type, beside the registrations. get_plugins_for_model keeps returning every registration, removed ones included: nothing declared is deleted. resolve() drops the named candidates.

registry.remove(model, plugin) accepts a plugin class or a name. It is exported as plugins.remove beside plugins.register (fairdm/contrib/plugins/__init__.py, which resolves names lazily: follow how `register` is exported). It records the declaration and validates nothing about the target when called, because the target may not be registered yet (FR-028). Whether it works is judged by resolve().

resolve() step 2: each removal must name a registration on that record type, or PluginRegistrationError naming the removal and the record type (FR-029). A removal of the record type's overview is refused with a message saying the overview can be replaced but not removed (FR-030). The overview is the registration that either is built on OverviewPlaces or has a url_path of None. Do not use the address alone: a sample's overview is served at overview/ beneath the sample, not at the sample's own address (fairdm/core/sample/plugins.py), and removing it would break Sample.get_absolute_url. Test both a project and a sample. (US4 will add: 'and states no `replaces`'. Write the rule so that clause can be added.)

The refusal messages are built by _fail in checks.py, which writes '<plugin> registered against <Model>: <problem>'. For a removal that sentence reads wrongly. Give removals their own wording that names the removal, the record type and the problem, still a PluginRegistrationError.
validate_all() resolves every record type that has a declaration: a record type with a removal and no registration must be resolved too, so the removal is refused.
A removed card's further views are not served either: no mount means no patterns. Card.admits finds the overview through resolve(), which is unaffected.

plan D7, shipped links. plugins.reverse (utils.py) gains default=: when given, NoReverseMatch returns it; when not given it raises as today. {% plugin_url %} in fairdm/contrib/plugins/templatetags/plugin_tags.py returns '' when the name does not resolve; the older plugin_url tag in fairdm/templatetags/fairdm.py does the same.

Shipped links to fix, found by the design review (verify each against the code, and search for more: plugin_reverse, plugins.reverse, {% plugin_url %}, safe_reverse, and plain reverse or {% url %} with a record namespace): (1) RecordOverviewPlugin.get_context_data in fairdm/core/plugins.py asks for 'contribution-list' for the People card. (2) fairdm/contrib/contributors/plugins/shared.py links to the Contributors page of the record ABOVE this one in two places (search for reverse(source, 'contribution-list') and reverse(parents[0], 'contribution-list')): with the plugin removed from Project, every dataset's Contributors page raises today. Both ask with default='' and contribution_list.html leaves out the button and the link when the address is empty. (3) Entries fed by safe_reverse, which returns None: the Manage menu in sample_overview.html (edit, basic-information, keywords, key-dates), project_detail.html (dataset-list, contribution-list links), dataset_detail.html, measurement's overview template, and person.html and organization.html (contributor-projects, contributor-datasets). Each entry is drawn only when it has an address. overview-update and overview-delete are further views of the overview, which cannot be removed, so they need nothing. (4) Templates that use {% plugin_url %}. A template nothing includes or extends any more is left alone: confirm before editing one, and list in your report any you found unused.

A stats tile or card whose link is gone still shows its figure; only the link is dropped. If a component takes an href and draws an anchor regardless, pass nothing rather than an empty string where the component already copes with that; do not edit django-mvp's components.

T011's list of removable plugins is read from the registry inside the test (every registration on every record type that is not the overview), so a plugin added later is covered. For each: remove it through the sandbox, open that record type's overview as a visitor and as someone who can manage the record, assert 200, no link to the former address, and no anchor whose href is empty or 'None'. Plus the cross-record cases: contribution-list removed from Project, then a dataset's Contributors page as a manager and as a visitor; removed from Dataset, then a sample's Contributors page.
Page tests use the plugin_sandbox fixture from tests/conftest.py (decisions.md D11). Give it a way to declare a removal, and make it restore removals on close.
Tests of the registry's removal behaviour go in tests/test_contrib/test_plugins/test_registration.py as new classes (TestRemove, TestRemoveRefusals): the test module mirrors registration.py.

docs/portal-development/create_a_plugin.md has one sentence under 'A feature that is more than one page' saying an additional view inherits its plugin's `check`. That is not how pages behave: a further view of a page is decided by its own check and permission, as the worked example further down that page and the comment in fairdm/core/project/plugins.py say. Correct that sentence in T013 so the page agrees with itself and with the card section story 2 wrote.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a registry filled by the test, when a plugin in each of the three places is removed from one record type, then it has no mount, pattern, entry, action or card there, still has them on another record type, the result does not depend on whether remove or register came first, get_plugins_for_model still returns the registration, and validate_all refuses a removal of something not registered and a removal of the overview of a project and of a sample, the latter saying it can be replaced.

Given each removable plugin FairDM registers, when it is removed from a record type and that record type's overview is opened as a visitor and as a manager, then the page answers 200 with no link to the former address and no anchor with an empty or None address; the former address answers 404 like an unknown one; the name does not reverse; and a dataset's and a sample's Contributors pages are served when the plugin is removed from the record type above.
Given the failing tests from T010 and T011, when the implementation lands, then all pass and every test that existed at the base passes unchanged.

Given create_a_plugin.md, when read against the branch, then it says how to remove a plugin with an example that runs, what happens to its address and name, that the overview cannot be removed, what the removal refusals are, that a link to another plugin should allow for its removal with reverse(..., default=''), and the sentence about additional views inheriting a check is corrected.
